>  * Running with "Custom Window" makes so that no window is embedded at all.

You mean setting the dropdown to "Custom Window" and leaving the title blank? On Windows it results in the Main Window getting embedded:

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/50fdc49e-24a9-4bbf-af10-7d16112edabe)

However, if you put some string into the custom window title field then this might be the expected result on Linux until someone (probably @Hilderin ) matches the Windows implementation and verifies it in a future PR :)

I see. Then this leaves only the empty "Game" tab then.
However, until the implementation for GNU/Linux is made, it should ignore the behavior and just keep embedding the root window for now.

@YeldhamDev Understood. I've updated the code to fix the tab switching issue now, and introduced a new Display Server feature called `FEATURE_SUBWINDOW_EMBEDDING` to handle the difference on Linux and other platforms that haven't caught up yet. The easiest path was to just hide the window selector dropdown and enforce GameView to always embed the main view, hopefully that works as a stopgap for now. Note for whoever implements the Linux side of things: you'll need to first enable the feature in the X11 display server code in order to test subwindow embedding properly.

Feel free to give a try and let me know if this looks better!

Yup it was discussed in the proposal here: https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/11091 The work needed for that is definitely something a future PR should handle, but I've got ideas on how to tackle it after this. In short, we could send a debugger signal to create a Window Node with a custom name and reuse the embedded subwindow functionality to set the intended window name to that window. Next step after that would be activating the debugger for the top view so that either can be used for debugging, but that definitely requires a new PR. We'd either need to make the game debugger code instantiable (so there can be 2 copies of it) or send the window name along with each signal so that the debugger can act depending on which view the user interacted with; either option should work from what I can tell.

> This one is probably beyond just a suggestion, but in addition to the `Debug Window`, I wonder if we could have a `Scene View` option, which would show the Scene viewport, like Unity. No idea if this is actually technically possible at this point, but something to wonder about. Something like this (mockup):

I could see that being useful, though users have to make sure they don't confuse the Scene View with the debug view - I'm thinking eventually (hopefully) we will have a lot of the same tools for runtime editing like the transform gizmos, so it will be important to distinguish them for beginners who may expect the Scene View to also work in runtime like in Unity. Side note: if it was up to me, I'd prefer an approach different than window embedding in the first place to get the editor tools at runtime, but considering this is what we've got, I'll work with it lol. 

Anyways, I think the long term solution to this would be something like https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/7233 where any viewport can be moved to any position, including the game tab views and 3D plugin so that users can make any layout they want. This is a lot of work but honestly it would probably be better to look into this than to try and figure out all the combinations of side-by-side windows that users might want. That's just my personal take though and if it's too far away, we can work with these alternatives for now

Does this PR also enable embedding two run instances of a game within the Godot Editor? If not, I'd like to kindly request that. ### Here's my usecase: I'm building a mobile game with multiplayer ([using the fantastic EOSG plugin](https://godotengine.org/asset-library/asset/2453)) and frequently have to debug/test with two run instances. The first instance/session gets embedded in the Godot Editor window, but the second one remains a floating window: Doing anything in the editor will move it to the front, hiding the floating window. This results in obscene amounts Alt+Tabbing. It would be amazing if the game view provided options for displaying multiple run instances/sessions, with the horizontal/vertical splits from this PR. To be really feature complete, this would probably need to be able to handle more than two sessions as well... I wouldn't mind iterating on the PR, if that's welcome.

@Robert-K If both instances are run from the editor, it may in fact be possible if you use the _Custom Window_ setting and provide a unique window name for each instance. All that's really happening is Godot attaching a special flag to the build telling it that if a window spawns with the given name, it should become parented, and then the `GameView` searches for it and takes control. Theoretically, any Godot window can work, but it's been a while and I may be misremembering some technical oversight like if the code grabbing the window requires a specific process ID... which will definitely be a problem for that.

If it doesn't work automatically then it should probably be addressed in a follow up PR as its not covered in the original proposal. This one is already a lot of changes and it's been hard to keep it up to date haha. On that note, I'll get around to rebasing it soon and hope to get more code reviews now that we're in 4.6 territory :)

CC @bruvzg to review the general DisplayServer and platform-specific parts, and @deralmas to check that it works on Wayland.

Regarding Wayland-ability, I think that this should work, with the necessary embedder changes. Worst case, the API can always be adjusted, as it's not exposed to games FWIU.

Talking about exposed API though, I wonder, is this new `p_parent` field of `create_sub_window` exposed to games? I can see that there are no changes to the binding code and no new docs so I assume that it's silently called with the default?

> Regarding Wayland-ability, I think that this should work, with the necessary embedder changes. Worst case, the API can always be adjusted, as it's not exposed to games FWIU.

Awesome that's good to hear, and when the Wayland implementation is looked at the `FEATURE_SUBWINDOW_EMBEDDING` display server flag should be enabled so that the editor knows to turn on the UI for it. Not sure how easy it is to replicate the Windows code but it's a small change so hopefully not too bad!

> Talking about exposed API though, I wonder, is this new `p_parent` field of `create_sub_window` exposed to games? I can see that there are no changes to the binding code and no new docs so I assume that it's silently called with the default?

Correct, it's not exposed to games. When the editor runs a debugging build of the game with intent to embed a subwindow, it passes the `--swid` flag in the command line params which is picked up by Core, which then stores a list of subwindows to embed. When a subwindow is created, it checks if the name matches something in the list and if so adds in the `p_parent` when calling the display server code. This is basically the same as how it works with the regular `--wid` flag used by main window embedding. Theoretically, a user could create a window at runtime via code that has the same name as one passed from the `--swid` flag and get that embedded (so long as the editor waits long enough to check for it), but that could be a useful feature for some projects

Thank you for the explanation, now I understand it a lot better :D

Interestingly, since on Wayland we intercept window creation messages, the embedding is done by the editor, you could say. That means that we should either add some control logic to the client, which right now is basically unmodified, or perhaps signal to the `DisplayServer` about the list of names to automatically embed.

Also, do I understand correctly that the "to-embed" list is pre-determined at startup and that windows are embedded only on creation? Right now I've always assumed that things could switch up on the fly, but if that were not the case it would make things a lot easier.

> Also, do I understand correctly that the "to-embed" list is pre-determined at startup and that windows are embedded only on creation? Right now I've always assumed that things could switch up on the fly, but if that were not the case it would make things a lot easier.

Yup! The Core checks for window names based on `--swid` at startup and that's the only system affecting the list for now at least. Windows are only embedded on creation because the relevant display server for the platform sets the "window parent" at that time. In order for embedding to happen, the window both needs the parent set when it spawns in and the special secret magic sauce contained within `embed_process` to be run targeting that window. I don't remember how that magic is done exactly, but thankfully the Windows platform's `embed_process` works on a generic window handle that I was able to set to a desired subwindow when the function is provided a name via `p_embedded_window` :)

I think `embed_process` is always run from from the editor as you've mentioned (check editor/run/embedded_process.cpp), but it might have some repeated attempt period where it tries to connect to a window. So if I'm understanding right, Wayland would just have to make sure that subwindows receive a parent when created, though I would've thought this would be set up for you already when this line happens:

```window_id = DisplayServer::get_singleton()->create_sub_window```

In scene/main/window.cpp, as I've already modified `create_sub_window` in Wayland display server to pass in the p_parent to make it compile (I didn't change any code, just the signature)

EDIT: And Wayland will also need the `embed_process` and `remove_embedded_process` changes too

> Yup! The Core checks for window names based on --swid at startup and that's the only system affecting the list for now at least. Windows are only embedded on creation because the relevant display server for the platform sets the "window parent" at that time.

Ohhh that's great news, then it will take a lot less work hopefully to port it to the Wayland embedder :D

> So if I'm understanding right, Wayland would just have to make sure that subwindows receive a parent when created, though I would've thought this would be set up for you already when this line happens:

That's the thing, we can't control "foreign" windows, _normally_ at least. That's part of Wayland's design, and it allows for weird new features and whatnot.

The details are _long_ (if you're curious, you can check #107435), but in short we solve this by intercepting the embedded game's requests and mess with its windows without it even knowing. This works because we can change the game's environment variables before spawning it.

That's why I say that the editor does the embedding, we have our own blend of magic for embedding, completely different from the Windows/X11 backend.

That said, yea, I think it's safe to say that with this approach it's more a matter of elbow grease than anything, and it shouldn't take that much time either :D

> Not sure I understand, are you saying it only makes "native windows" and creating 2 "native windows" not possible for some reason?

Currently, macOS has two fully separate display server implementations:
- one is a normal GUI app that can create native windows.
- another one (this one used for embedded game) is non-gui app that can't create any windows (or directly interact with the user) at all, and use shared framebuffer to send rendered content to the editor / network sockets to receive input from editor.

So it can be easily updated to embed multiple windows, but can't have embedded and non-embedded window, to support this we'll need to merge both implementations, which is non-trivial.

Embedding in the way Windows do it (attaching one process native window to another process window) is not possible due to OS restrictions.

> so hopefully that's okay for now and once this is all set in stone we could see what's possible there.

Yes, it's OK to have it implement for Windows only for now.
